title: Sliding Window Thermalization and Tenant Cohorting for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-level PRD for a capacity orchestration feature that smooths the activation/deactivation of reserved slots (thermalization) over a sliding time window and groups tenants into dynamic cohorts that can safely share ephemeral headroom. This aims to reduce oscillation, lower preemptive evictions, and improve utilization while preserving isolation guarantees for high-tier customers.
problem_statement: Dedicated pools occasionally experience sharp oscillations in active slot usage due to synchronous tenant bursts and aggressive autoscale reactions, leading to avoidable preemptions and degradation for reserved tenants.
Current hard cutoff or immediate reclaim policies either waste capacity (overprovisioning) or cause noisy neighbor effects and SLA violations when many tenants spike simultaneously.
We lack a simple, observable control that lets operators tune the transient behavior between responsiveness and stability for reserved pools.
There is also no standardized way to let low-priority tenants safely borrow short-lived headroom from compatible peers without complex manual policies.
goals: Design and implement a sliding-window thermalizer that ramps reservation activation/deactivation over configurable time windows to avoid oscillations.
Implement tenant cohorting logic that groups compatible tenants (based on burst profile, priority, and model footprint) to enable controlled ephemeral sharing of headroom with isolation constraints.
Expose operator controls (window length, ramp rate, cohort tolerance) in Console and via API, with strong telemetry for tuning.
Provide rollback-safe rollout and canary for a subset of pools and tenants.
Define clear acceptance criteria and SLO impact thresholds before general availability.
non_goals: This PRD does not propose a full rewrite of the autoscaler or tenant billing model.
We will not change hard SLA commitments for enterprise reserved customers in this phase; cohorts may be limited to P2/P3 reservations and opportunistic capacity.
We will not introduce model-level kernel selection changes as part of thermalization — this is orthogonal and handled by runtime.
detailed_spec: Thermalization engine: when a tenant's reserved allocation changes (scale up/down or ephemeral borrow), apply a ramp with configurable shape (linear, exponential) across a sliding window T. The engine enforces partial activation percentages during ramp to limit instant concurrency increases.

Cohorting classifier: service will compute tenant similarity scores from historical burst metrics (peak QPS, burst duration, avg sequence length) and tenancy priority. Cohorts are dynamic and recomputed hourly by default.

Borrow policy: within a cohort, lower-priority tenants may request ephemeral headroom up to 'cohort_headroom_pct' of idle capacity. Requests are soft-granted with preemption hooks and a two-phase commit to avoid scheduling races.

Isolation constraints: always keep a min_protected_capacity per high-tier tenant that cannot be borrowed. Cohort borrowing triggers immediate telemetry events and per-tenant throttling if preemption rate exceeds threshold.
API: add POST /pools/:id/thermalization/config and GET /pools/:id/cohorts to Console API. New fields: window_seconds, ramp_shape, cohort_tolerance, cohort_headroom_pct, min_protected_capacity.

Console UX: a simple slider for window length, dropdown for ramp shape, cohort preview view showing proposed groupings and estimated available headroom, and a simulation tool to run a synthetic burst and show predicted evictions.

Telemetry and alerts: emit metrics for ramp_in_progress, cohort_rebalance_count, ephemeral_borrows, preemptions_by_cause. Add dashboard with fairness and eviction heatmaps and alert if preemption rate > 0.5% of requests over 15m for reserved tenants.
Rollout: start with one non-critical zone and a single low-risk pool (P2 seats), run 2-week soak, expand to other pools if metrics stable. Provide feature flag to disable per-pool.
api_and_contract_changes: New pool config schema fields: window_seconds (integer), ramp_shape (string enum: linear|exp), cohorting_enabled (boolean), cohort_tolerance (float 0-1), cohort_headroom_pct (float), min_protected_capacity (integer).
Backward compatible: defaults must preserve current behavior (window_seconds=0 => immediate activation; cohorting_enabled=false).
Add events: THERMALIZER_RAMP_START, THERMALIZER_RAMP_END, COHORT_BORROW_GRANTED, COHORT_BORROW_PREEMPTED.
security_and_compliance: No sensitive data is introduced; cohort selection uses aggregated metrics only.
Audit logs must capture ephemeral borrow grants and preemptions for compliance customers; add audit flag to pool config to force logging.
Security review required before GA for changes to preemption signalling (security_review_required=true).
dependencies: Runtime: support for partial activation slices per reservation (ENG-12522)
Autoscaler: expose hooks to accept delayed scale actions (ENG-13210)
Telemetry pipeline: new metrics and events (ENG-14003)
Billing: confirm ephemeral borrow cost attribution (PM-92011)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Misconfigured window may increase latency for bursty workloads. Mitigation: provide conservative defaults (10s window), simulation tool, and canary rollout.
Risk: Cohort classifier could group incompatible tenants causing noisy neighbor. Mitigation: cohort_tolerance floor and manual overrides; initial rollout restricts cohorts to same billing tier.
Risk: Telemetry overload from high-frequency events. Mitigation: sampling and aggregated counters; opt-in debug mode.
metrics_and_success_criteria: P99 latency for reserved tenants does not regress more than 5% compared to baseline during 99th percentile bursts.
Preemptions for reserved tenants reduce by 40% in pools with thermalizer enabled (measured over 14-day window) relative to historical baseline.
Average utilization of dedicated pools increases by at least 6% without exceeding peak latency thresholds.
Cohort borrow churn (borrow grant followed by preemption within 60s) under 1% of borrows in steady-state.
Operator can toggle thermalization per-pool and view cohort composition in Console; simulation predictions match observed behavior within 15% error on synthetic tests.
acceptance_criteria: API and Console controls implemented and documented in PRD + Console help doc.
Thermalizer ramp logic passes unit and integration tests including race conditions test harness.
Cohort classifier results are visible in Console with ability to lock cohorts; at least 3 telemetry dashboards exist (ramp, cohorts, preemptions) with alerts wired.
Canary run for 2 weeks in staging and then 2 production pools with all success metrics met; rollback plan documented.
Security review completed and audit logging enabled for pools flagged for compliance.
rollout_and_migration_plan: Phase 0: Implement server-side feature flag and API changes; unit/integration tests (2 weeks).
Phase 1: Console UI + simulation + internal docs; sandbox testing and UX feedback (1 week).
Phase 2: Canary rollout to one non-critical pool for 14 days; monitor metrics daily and run synthetic burst tests (2 weeks).
Phase 3: Expand to up to 10 pools across zones if criteria met; continue gradual expansion with weekly review.
Migration: existing pools retain window_seconds=0 unless explicitly opted-in; provide a guided wizard in Console to recommend settings based on historical patterns.
open_questions: What is the optimal default window_seconds for multi-tenant heavy-tailed workloads? Initial proposal: 10s, but requires A/B testing.
Should cohorts be limited to same customer billing tier for GA? Proposed: yes for first release.
How will billing attribution appear for ephemeral borrows—line-item or amortized? Need finance input (PM-92011).
notes: This design is intentionally conservative to avoid SLA risk for P0/P1 reserved customers.
